name: dsh-focus-free-shortcuts
description: Local runtime patch: make the right-Sidebar pane commands (fullscreen primary+alt+Enter, split primary+Backslash), the double-Escape turn stop, and the approval panel's Enter/Escape decision fire without first clicking into the pane, the composer, or the approval card. Every bundled owner resolves its target from the keydown event target, and a keydown is dispatched to the focused element (or <body> when nothing is focused), so all of them silently decline until the user focuses the exact region: `pane.fullscreen.toggle` / `pane.split` call SidebarRight.focusedTarget(element) and return command.noFocus; the fixed `response.stop` sequence requires its target inside [data-conversation-session] / [data-conversation-region]; and the approval panel answers only while document.activeElement sits inside [data-approval-key] — which the composer takeover removes when it hides the composer bar, so focus falls back to <body> and both Enter and Escape lose their owner. This plugin opens its own fixed-input observer — the channel that runs for every keydown before configurable dispatch and can consume the press — and resolves the same owner without DOM focus: SidebarRight.commandTarget()'s active-dock-pane fallback for the pane commands, the main-view Session for the stop (`sessions.list.byId[id].retainedBy.mainView > 0`, the same fact UiSession uses), and that Session's published `pendingInteraction` approval for Enter/Escape (`answer('allowed-once' | 'rejected')`, the operation the panel buttons call). It consumes a press only when it actually acts, and stands down whenever the bundled owner owns that press (focused pane, conversation region, `[data-approval-key]` subtree), so exactly one owner remains per press. Nothing is registered in the shortcut catalog: no default bindings, no conflicts, no settings edits — and because each bridge follows the effective catalog row or the mounted fixed row, a rebound, unbound, or absent bundled command is left alone (an unmounted approval plugin removes approval.allow / approval.reject and the approval bridge becomes a no-op). Pane keys are Web-runtime only: Desktop dispatches configurable bindings from its native bridge, where a DOM-side consume cannot suppress the bundled press; the stop and approval keys are fixed actions and install on both runtimes.
